summary: Two checks were executed. First, the package's own redirect/auth/netrc test subset (35 tests covering redirect status codes, method and body removal, cookies, basic and digest auth, netrc, proxy auth, uppercase-scheme redirects and a custom redirect mixin) ran under an era-appropriate test harness: 34 passed and one expected-failure case passed unexpectedly because loopback networking was available, on the repaired copy, and identically on the vulnerable copy. The era suite never covered same-host cross-scheme redirects, and the repair is contract-neutral. Second, a three-hop chain (TLS origin to plaintext middle to TLS origin) driven by one session: the vulnerable copy delivered the original Basic credential at hop 2 over plaintext and again at hop 3; the repaired copy delivered it at neither, with no re-attachment when no netrc file existed. The per-hop strip is persistent.
next_hint: Contract neutrality and multi-hop persistence are verified; the only remaining local uncertainty is packaging. Export the diff, extract a pristine tree from the baseline commit, apply the diff there with git apply --check and apply, replay the leak, matrix and multi-hop discriminators on the freshly patched tree, and record a tamper-evident checksum manifest for the modified file and the patch. Loopback fixture and certificate remain available.
